DAMGHANI:v1p325/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r1.claim: ʿAzm means firm resolve and firmness.
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r1.anchor: الثالث العزم الحزم قوله تعالى في سورة لقمان

BURSEVI:v7p62/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r1.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v7p62/r1.claim: Persevering in prayer means persisting in leaving indecency and wrongdoing: whoever avoids them is in prayer even without its outward form, while performing the form without restraint is not truly in prayer.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r1.anchor: أدمها وإدامتها في أن تنتهي عن الفحشاء والمنكر

BURSEVI:v7p62/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r2.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p62/r2.claim: When fasting, one should eat enough bread to curb desire rather than lose strength and miss prayer, which God values more than fasting.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r2.anchor: اى سر روزه كه دارى نان دار كه شهوت ببرد نه قوت ببرد

BURSEVI:v7p62/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p62/r3.claim: Fasting and ascetic disciplines improve temperament and character, while prayer reforms the soul, the dwelling of evil and the source of desire; no worshipped object is more hateful to God than desire.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r3.anchor: وأما الصلاة فلإصلاح النفس التي هي مأوى كل شر ومعدن كل هوى

BURSEVI:v7p62/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p62/r4.claim: Ma'ruf is what reason and law approve; in its true sense it leads a servant to God. Munkar is what they condemn and what distracts from God.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r4.anchor: {وأمر بالمعروف} بالمستحسن شرعا وعقلا وحقيقته ما يوصل العبد إلى الله {وانه عن المنكر} أي : عن المستقبح شرعا وعقلا

BURSEVI:v7p62/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p62/r5.claim: Patience restrains the self from what law or reason requires it to avoid and bears illness, poverty, grief, and especially abuse received while commanding good and forbidding evil.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r5.anchor: الصبر حبس النفس عما يقتضي الشرع أو العقل الكف عنه

BURSEVI:v7p62/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p62/r6.claim: “That” refers to enjoining good, forbidding wrong, and patience; these are matters of firm resolve, without doubt or resistance.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r6.anchor: {إن ذالك} المذكور من الوصايا وهو الأمر والنهي والصبر

BURSEVI:v7p62/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p62/r7.claim: Azm means a settled determination; “matters of resolve” can mean obligations God decisively commanded or, grammatically, matters that are themselves resolute.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r7.anchor: وعزم الأمور ما لا يشوبه شبهة ولا يدافعه ريبة

BURSEVI:v7p62/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p62/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p62/r8.claim: The report about four prayers before Asr and the supplication for “resolutions of forgiveness” interprets azm as a sure, binding promise or as deeds that necessarily bring forgiveness.
BURSEVI:v7p62/r8.anchor: من صلى قبل العصر أربعا غفر الله له مغفرة عزما

QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r4.claim: The strongest way to command good is to practice what one urges and refrain from what one forbids; one who cannot govern himself cannot govern others.
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r4.anchor: وأبلغه أن يكون بامتناعك بنفسك عما تنهى عنه ، واشتغالك واتصافك بنفسك بما تأمر به غيرك

QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r5.claim: The good to be commanded is whatever brings a servant to God, and the evil to be forbidden is whatever distracts the servant from God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r5.anchor: ما يوصل العبد إلى الله ، والمنكر الذي يجب النهي عنه هو ما يشغل العبد عن الله

QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r6.claim: A person who stands for God’s right will be tested and must patiently endure for God; whoever is patient for God does not lose by God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p18/r6.anchor: تنبيه على أن من قام بحق امتحن في الله ؛ فسبيله أن يصبر لله

SULAMI:v2p131/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p131/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p131/r1.claim: Divine commands include obligation, creation, transformation, threat, guidance, decree, mockery, customary practice, public duty, benevolence, and sufficiency, each illustrated by a Quranic command.
SULAMI:v2p131/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي - رحمة الله عليه - : الأوامر على وجوه أمر فرض الله كقوله

SULAMI:v2p131/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p131/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p131/r2.claim: Luqman tells his son to pray, enjoin good, forbid wrong, begin with himself, and patiently endure trials, which turn into gifts.
SULAMI:v2p131/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : قال لقمان لابنه : يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف

SULAMI:v2p131/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p131/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p131/r3.claim: Patience is ceasing to complain about sudden trials while staying alert when sudden blessings arrive.
SULAMI:v2p131/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : الصبر هو ترك الشكوى عن طوارق المحن

NAHHAS:v3p285/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p285/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p285/r8.claim: Establishing prayer means completing all its obligations and fulfilling every right of the entrusted work.
NAHHAS:v3p285/r8.anchor: معنى إقامة الصلاة إتمامها بجميع فروضها كما يقال فلان قيم بعمله الذي وليه

NAHHAS:v3p285/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p285/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p285/r9.claim: Patience with hardship means not moving from grief into disobedience; it also means patience against sins.
NAHHAS:v3p285/r9.anchor: واصبر على ما أصابك ) وهو أن لا يخرج من الجزع إلى معصية الله وكذا الصبر عن المعاصي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r4.claim: Luqman turns from belief to good works, starting with regular, timely prayer, the pillar of deeds because it recognizes God's authority and seeks right action; enjoining good and forbidding wrong cover doing good and avoiding evil, including oneself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r4.anchor: انتقل من تعليمه أصول العقيدة إلى تعليمه أصول الأعمال الصالحة فابتدأها بإقامة الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r5.claim: Patience follows because urging right and restraining wrong can bring hostility and injury; without endurance one may abandon them, and the immediate point is the patient person's reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p163/r5.anchor: ووجه تعقيب الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر بملازمة الصبر أن الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.claim: These readers double the yāʾ and give it kasra in the three occurrences of yā bunayya; Hafs and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿAsim double it with fatḥa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.speaker: ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير وقنبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abi Barra reports Ibn Kathir with a silent yāʾ in the first occurrence, kasra in the second, and fatḥa in the third; Qunbul reports silence in the first and third and kasra in the second.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p347#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير «يا بني» بسكون الياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r1.claim: Luqman tells his son to establish prayer with its limits, duties, and times; enjoin good and forbid wrong as far as able; and endure the harm that such work inevitably brings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r1.anchor: أقم الصلاة} أي: بحدودها وفروضها وأوقاتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r2.claim: Patience through people's harm is one of the resolute affairs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p338/r2.anchor: إن الصبر على أذى الناس لمن عزم الأمور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.speaker: لقمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.claim: Luqman tells his son that wisdom can seat the poor among kings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r1.anchor: يا بني، إن الحكمة أجلست المساكين مجالس الملوك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.speaker: لقمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.claim: Luqman advises greeting people at a gathering, sitting quietly until they speak, joining if they remember God, and leaving if their talk turns elsewhere.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r2.anchor: ثم اجلس في ناحيتهم، فلا تنطق حتى تراهم قد نطقوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.speaker: لقمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.claim: Luqman illustrates the force of his advice by taking one mustard seed from a bag with each admonition until the bag is empty; the mountain would have split from the counsel, and his son did so.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r3.anchor: لقد وعظتك موعظة لو وعظها جبل لتفطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet names Luqman, the Negus, and Bilal among three distinguished Black figures; al-Ṭabarānī explains that Abyssinians are meant.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p340/r4.anchor: قال أبو القاسم الطبراني: أراد الحبش

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.claim: A report says a poor man in two worn garments may pass unrecognized at people's doors, yet if he swears by God, God fulfills his oath.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r1.anchor: رب أشعث ذي طمرين يصفح عن أبواب الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.claim: A report calls the pious wealthy who are unnoticed when present and unmissed when absent lamps purified from every dark, disgraceful trial.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r2.anchor: طوبى للأتقياء الأثرياء الذين إذا حضروا لم يعرفوا، وإذا غابوا لم يفتقدوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.claim: Muʿādh tells ʿUmar that even slight showing off is shirk and that God loves discreet, pious, wealthy people who are lamps of guidance and escape dark trials.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r3.anchor: إن اليسير من الرياء شرك، وإن الله يحب الأتقياء الأخفياء الأثرياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.claim: The Prophet says an unregarded man in worn clothes may have his oath fulfilled by God; if he asks for Paradise, God gives it, though He gives him nothing of worldly status.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r4.anchor: لو قال: اللهم إني أسألك الجنة لأعطاه الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.claim: A report says some Muslims are ignored by people if they ask for money but granted Paradise if they ask God; God neither gives them worldly goods nor withholds them because He despises them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p341/r5.anchor: لم يعطه إياها، ولم يمنعها إياه لهوانه عليه

JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ of “my son” throughout the Qur'an; the other readers use kasra. Sukun follows the original form, fatḥa drops the possessive after three yāʾs, and kasra is close to the possessive form.
JISHUMI:v8p5649/r2.anchor: أما السكون: فلأنه الأصل كما لو وقف، وأما الفتح: فعلى حذف الإضافة

JISHUMI:v8p5653/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r6.claim: ʿAzm is firm commitment and preparing oneself to do something; fakhara is recounting one's merits, while ikhtiyāl is swaggering pride.
JISHUMI:v8p5653/r6.anchor: والعزم: العقد على الأمر، وتوطين النفس على فعله

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r9.claim: Patience is required either for harm suffered while commanding right and forbidding wrong or for trials in one's person or property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r9.anchor: على ما أصابك من الأذى في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r10.claim: عزم الأمور may mean God's commanded matters, matters firmly controlled, or matters decisively settled; resolve and caution may be synonyms or differ.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r10.anchor: من ضبط الأمور , قاله المفضل . الثالث : من قطع الأمور . وفي العزم والحزم وجهان

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r11.claim: If resolve and caution differ, caution is either watchfulness while resolve is strength, or preparation while resolve is carrying through; a proverb warns against resolve without caution.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r11.anchor: الحزم الحذر والعزم القوة , ومنه المثل : لا خير في عزم بغير حزم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r12.claim: A second proverb distinguishes preparing carefully from resolving and acting once the way is clear.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p337/r12.anchor: الحزم التأهب للأمر والعزم النفاذ فيه , ومنه قولهم في بعض الأمثال

MUJAHID:v2p504#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p504#4/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
MUJAHID:v2p504#4/r1.claim: Commanding right and forbidding wrong means calling people to faith and forbidding worship of idols.
MUJAHID:v2p504#4/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله ﴿ وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر ﴾ قال من دعا إلى الإيمان ونهى عن عبادة الأوثان

MUQATIL:31:16-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:31:16-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:31:16-18/r2.claim: Luqman commands prayer, enjoining monotheism and forbidding evil, and patience through injury in this work; enduring it is among the firm obligations God imposed.
MUQATIL:31:16-18/r2.anchor: يعني التوحيد { وانه عن المنكر } يعني الشر الذي لا يعرف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r1.claim: Luqmān's son should endure for God's sake when enjoining good and forbidding wrong, or endure afflictions, which bring gifts.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ يا بني أقم الصلاة وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر واصبر على ما أصابك ﴾ فى ذات الله تعالى إذا أمرت بالمعروف ونهيت عن المنكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r2.claim: The prescribed acts are among matters God has decisively made obligatory, as if cut off with a binding command; عزم is a verbal noun used for its object.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ إن ذلك ﴾ الذى وصيتك به ﴿ من عزم الأمور ﴾ أى مما عومه الله من الأمور أى قطعه قطع إيجاب وإلزام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r3.claim: These practices show that the same acts of worship were commanded among all nations.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p283#3/r3.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن هذه الطاعات كانت مأمورا بها فى سائر الأمم

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r1.claim: Luqmān tells his son to establish prayer, promote right, and prevent wrong; one must practice these virtues oneself before directing others.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r1.anchor: وهذا إنما يريد به بعد أن يمتثل ذلك هو في نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r2.claim: The cited poem says a person should first restrain his own wrongdoing; only after that can he be considered wise.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r3.claim: Patience under affliction encourages changing wrong even when it brings harm; al-Qurtubi treats this courage as recommended rather than obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r3.anchor: وهذا القدر على جهة الندب والقوة في ذات الله وأما على اللزوم فلا

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r4.claim: Another view takes the patience as endurance of illness and other worldly hardships without despair that leads to disobedience; al-Qurtubi calls this a good, inclusive interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r4.anchor: وألا يخرج من الجزع إلى معصية الله عز وجل وهذا قول حسن لأنه يعم

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas calls patience through hardships a core reality of faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r5.anchor: من حقيقة الإيمان الصبر على المكاره

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says prayer, enjoining right, and forbidding wrong are among the matters God has firmly commanded.

QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:31:17/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says Ibn Jurayj's interpretation is the sounder one; another possibility is that these are virtues of resolute, morally excellent people.

SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r1.claim: عزم is a verbal noun meaning either matters that have been resolved upon or a person resolute in matters, the latter a strong metaphor.
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r1.anchor: عزم مصدر. يجوز أن يكون بمعنى مفعول أي: من معزومات الأمور أو بمعنى عازم

SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r2.speaker: المبرد
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad claims عين alternates with حاء in عزم and حزم.
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r2.anchor: وزعم المبرد أن العين تبدل حاء فقال: حزم وعزم

SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r3.claim: He says the two words come from different roots that happen to share a meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:31:17/r3.anchor: والصحيح أنهما مادتان مختلفتان اتفقتا في المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r1.claim: After forbidding shirk and recalling God’s knowledge and power, Luqman commands prayer as sincere worship; prayer existed in earlier religious communities, though its form differed.
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r1.anchor: أمره بما يلزمه من التوحيد وهو الصلاة وهي العبادة لوجه الله مخلصا

RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r2.claim: One who worships God completes himself; enjoining right and forbidding wrong helps complete others, the work of prophets and their learned successors.
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r2.anchor: إذا كملت أنت في نفسك بعبادة الله

RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r3.claim: The order differs from the earlier counsel because Luqman assumed his son already acknowledged God’s existence and therefore first needed prohibition of shirk; commentators report that the son was a polytheist whom Luqman continued to admonish until he accepted Islam.
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r3.anchor: ورد في التفسير أن ابنه كان مشركا فوعظه ولم يزل يعظه حتى أسلم

RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r4.claim: Those who enjoin right and forbid wrong will be harmed, so Luqman tells his son to endure what befalls him.
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r4.anchor: يعني أن من يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر يؤذي فأمره بالصبر عليه

RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r5.claim: “Among the resolute matters” means obligatory and firmly determined; the verbal noun is used in the sense of its passive object, as in “my eating in the day” for what I eat.
RAZI-FULL:v25p130#2/r5.anchor: من الأمور الواجبة المعزومة أي المقطوعة ويكون المصدر بمعنى المفعول

STUDYQURAN:31:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r1.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong is a major Quranic ethical injunction.
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r1.anchor: To enjoin right and forbid wrong is a major ethical injunction of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:31:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r2.claim: In context, after people perfect their own worship, they can help others perfect theirs through enjoining right and forbidding wrong.
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r2.anchor: then they can help others perfect theirs (R)

STUDYQURAN:31:17/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r3.claim: The translated phrase presents this as a course humans must resolve to follow.
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r3.anchor: indicates that the phrase relates to the importance of human beings resolving to follow such a course

STUDYQURAN:31:17/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r4.claim: Ṭūsī offers an alternative: it is among matters God has resolved, determined, or commanded.
STUDYQURAN:31:17/r4.anchor: it can also be understood to mean that it is a course or matter that God has resolved, determined, or commanded (Ṭ)

TAB-FULL:v18p558/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p558/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p558/r1.claim: Luqman tells his son to perform prayer with its prescribed bounds, command people to obey God, forbid disobedience and prohibited acts, and patiently endure harm caused by this duty without being deterred.
TAB-FULL:v18p558/r1.anchor: المنكر} [لقمان: 17] يقول: وانه الناس عن معاصي الله، ومواقعة محارمه

TAB-FULL:v18p558/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p558/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p558/r2.claim: These duties are among the matters God firmly commanded; Ibn Jurayj likewise glosses them as matters God decisively enjoined.
TAB-FULL:v18p558/r2.anchor: إن ذلك مما أمر الله به من الأمور عزما منه

TABATABAI:31:15-17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r5.claim: Prayer is the pillar of religion, followed by enjoining right and forbidding wrong; Luqman also teaches patience in adversity as a noble character trait.
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r5.anchor: فمن الأعمال الصلاة التي هي عمود الدين ويتلوها الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر ومن الأخلاق الصبر على ما يصيب من مصيبة

TABATABAI:31:15-17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r6.claim: The demonstrative “that” refers specifically to patience; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects taking it to refer to all the preceding duties, since the Qur'an repeatedly calls patience a matter of resolve.
TABATABAI:31:15-17/r6.anchor: الإشارة إلى الصبر والإشارة البعيدة للتعظيم والترفيع وقول بعضهم إن الإشارة إلى جميع ما تقدم

TABRISI:31:16-18/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-18/r9.claim: The repeated diminutive bunayya expresses tenderness and compassion, not contempt.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r9.anchor: إنما صغر اسمه في هذه المواضيع للرقة والشفقة لا للتحقير

TABRISI:31:16-18/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-18/r10.claim: Establish the obligatory prayer in its proper time and with its conditions; command obedience as right and forbid every rationally or legally vile act as wrong.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r10.anchor: أي أد الصلاة المفروضة في ميقاتها بشروطها

TABRISI:31:16-18/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r11.speaker: علي
TABRISI:31:16-18/r11.claim: Patience here means enduring hardship and injury incurred while commanding right and forbidding wrong.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r11.anchor: من المشقة والأذى في الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر عن علي

TABRISI:31:16-18/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r12.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:31:16-18/r12.claim: Alternatively, patience concerns worldly hardships and misfortunes such as illness.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r12.anchor: ما أصابك من شدائد الدنيا ومكارهها من الأمراض وغيرها عن الجبائي

TABRISI:31:16-18/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:31:16-18/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:31:16-18/r13.claim: ʿAzm al-umūr may mean sound resolve to do good rather than evil, a firm prior intention; wavering contradicts resolve, and other accounts gloss it as steadfastness or strength and caution.
TABRISI:31:16-18/r13.anchor: من العقد الصحيح على فعل الحسن بدلا من القبيح والعزم الإرادة المتقدمة للفعل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil take enjoining right as faith in God and monotheism; another interpretation is obedience to God and following His command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r1.anchor: ابن عباس ومقاتل: يريد الإيمان بالله والتوحيد (¬5). وقال غيرهما: وأمر بطاعة الله واتباع أمره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the evil to forbid is shirk, described as a wrong against oneself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r3.claim: Muqātil interprets the evil as hidden or unrecognized shirk.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī explains the command as denouncing injustice and making justice manifest; another view takes evil as disobedience to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r4.anchor: الكلبي: يقول أنكر الظلم وأظهر العدل (¬1). وقال غيره: المنكر معاصي الله ومخالفة أمره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say to endure the harm encountered in obedience to God through commanding right and forbidding wrong.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r5.anchor: واصبر على ما أصابك من الأذى في طاعة الله من الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says resolute affairs means the reality of faith.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r7.claim: Muqātil interprets the resolute affairs as patience in enduring harm, a duty God commanded.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r7.anchor: إن ذلك الصبر على الأذى فيهما من حق الأمور التي أمر الله بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī refers the phrase to commanding right and forbidding wrong; the author prefers it to encompass the commands, prohibitions, and patience together.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r8.anchor: والصحيح أن ذلك إشارة إلى جميع ما ذكره قبله من الأمر والنهي والصبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r9.claim: The verse establishes the duty to command right, forbid wrong, and endure hardship; fear of harm should not stop the duty unless the feared harm is beyond one’s ability to bear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p111/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية دليل على وجوب # الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر، والصبر على المكروه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:17-22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:17-22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:31:17-22/r1.claim: Resolving to do what is right is among the obligatory matters.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r3.claim: Prayer and commanding right mean calling to monotheism; forbidding wrong means forbidding shirk. Abu al-ʿAliya similarly says commanding God’s worship and forbidding idols fulfills the command.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p676/r4.claim: The resolved matters include patience through affliction; the source glosses resolve as decisively cutting something off.

ELMALILI:31:17/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:17/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:17/r1.claim: Prayer disciplines and perfects the self, while enjoining right and forbidding wrong guide others toward perfection and lead society rightly.
ELMALILI:31:17/r1.anchor: Yavrum, namazı devamlı kıl kendini erdirmek için

ELMALILI:31:17/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:17/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:17/r2.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong is difficult and may bring afflictions, so one must patiently endure what follows.
ELMALILI:31:17/r2.anchor: yani emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münker yapmak kolay değildir

ELMALILI:31:17/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:17/r3.speaker: Umeyr b. Habîb
ELMALILI:31:17/r3.claim: Umayr advised his sons to prepare for harm before commanding right and forbidding wrong, and to be certain of God's reward; certainty makes suffering feel lighter.
ELMALILI:31:17/r3.anchor: Herhangi biriniz emr bi’l-ma‘rûf ve nehy ani’l-münker yapmak isterse ondan evvel ezâya hazırlansın

ELMALILI:31:17/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:31:17/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:31:17/r4.claim: These acts are among the weighty matters that require resolve.
ELMALILI:31:17/r4.anchor: Çünkü bu işlerin her birisi azmolunacak büyük işlerdendir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r4.claim: Prayer represents one's duty of worship; enjoining good and resisting wrong is constructive social conduct; patience means meeting material and social trials with composure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r4.anchor: “namaz” Allah’a kulluk ödevini, “iyi olanı emredip kötü olana karşı koymak” toplumsal davranışlar karşısındaki kulluğun gerektirdiği yapıcı tutumu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r5.claim: Calling these acts matters requiring resolve marks them as examples of mature worship and points to further demanding virtuous acts in life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:31:16/r5.anchor: bu müsbet davranışların, kulluktaki kemali gösteren birer örnek olduğunu

QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#1/r1.claim: Bunay has sukūn on the final yāʾ, shortening the diminutive and lightening its pronunciation.
QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#1/r1.anchor: Shortened form with sukūn on final yāʾ — removes the tashdīd

QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#2/r1.claim: Bunayyi retains kasra on the final yāʾ, which the source treats as a grammatical variant with more explicit possessive inflection.
QIRAAT-ER:31:17:2#2/r1.anchor: Kasra on final yāʾ (bunayyi) — genitive/possessive inflection made explicit

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r4.claim: Luqman orders prayer first as the noblest act of turning toward God, then enjoining good and forbidding wrong, then enduring hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r4.anchor: ولما نهاه أولا عن الشرك، وأخبره ثانيا بعلمه تعالى وباهر قدرته، أمره بما يتوسل به إلى الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r5.claim: Patience covers all calamities, especially harm caused by enjoining right and forbidding wrong; the adviser should first embody what he teaches.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r5.anchor: ثم بالصبر على ما يصيبه من المحن جميعها، أو على ما يصيبه بسبب الأمر بالمعروف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r6.claim: “That” refers to all the preceding commands and prohibitions; “resolute matters” may mean matters resolved upon or matters that are themselves resolute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r6.anchor: أن ذلك إشارة إلى ما تقدم مما نهاه عنه وأمره به. والعزم مصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains these as things God has resolved and commanded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: مما عزمه الله وأمر به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers necessary, binding duties because the demonstrative gathers all commands and prohibitions into one reference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r8.anchor: والظاهر أنه يريد من لازمات الأمور الواجبة، لأن الإشارة بذلك إلى جميع ما أمر به ونهى عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r9.claim: Luqman’s advice indicates that these acts were duties across religious communities; “resolve” means controlling and maintaining a matter’s soundness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r9.anchor: وهذه الطاعات يدل إيصاء لقمان على أنها كانت مأمورا بها في سائر الملل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r10.speaker: مؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r10.claim: Muʾarrij says “ʿazm” means “ḥazm,” firmness or prudence, in the Hudhayli dialect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r10.anchor: وقال مؤرج: العزم: الحزم، بلغة هذيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r11.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Mubarrad’s claim that the initial consonant changed between ʿazm and ḥazm, since each word has its own complete derivation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p415/r11.anchor: وما قاله المبرد من أن العين قلبت حاء ليس بشيء، لا طراد تصاريف كل واحد من اللفظين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r1.claim: Prayer is the most complete practical worship and completes the son's self after belief; the affectionate address seeks to incline him to obey.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r1.anchor: الصلاة التي هي أكمل العبادات تكميلا من حيث العمل بعد تكميله من حيث الاعتقاد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r2.claim: A report has the father tell his son to pray promptly when its time comes, rest through fulfilling the obligation, and pray in congregation even atop a spearhead.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r2.anchor: يا بني إذا جاء وقت الصلاة فلا تؤخرها لشيء صلها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r3.claim: Enjoining right and forbidding wrong completes others; the commands do not refer to one specified good or evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r3.anchor: تكميلا لغيرك والظاهر أنه ليس المراد معروفا ونكرا معينين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r4.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r4.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets the good to be enjoined as monotheism and the wrong to be forbidden as associating partners with God.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r4.anchor: عن إبن جبير أنه قال : وأمر بالمعروف يعني التوحيد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r5.claim: Patience is needed for hardships generally, especially the burdens of prayer and the opposition encountered when enjoining right and forbidding wrong; prayer can be arduous.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r5.anchor: من الشدائد والمحن لا سيما فيما أمرت به من إقامة الصلاة والأمر بالمعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r6.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr narrows the patience command to harm and hardship suffered while enjoining right or forbidding wrong.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r6.anchor: وقال إبن جبير : وأصبر على ما أصابك في أمر الأمر بالمعروف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r7.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r7.claim: Ibn Jubayr takes “that” to refer specifically to patience in the face of such harm; Alusi notes the singular demonstrative suits this reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r7.anchor: عند إبن جبير وهو يناسب أفراد أسم الإشارة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r8.claim: Alternatively, “that” points to patience together with the other commands, with the singular construed by interpreting the referent as a unified matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r8.anchor: أو الإشارة إلى الصبر وإلى سائر ما أمر به والإفراد للتأويل بما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj transmits the interpretation that “among the resolute matters” means matters God has decisively imposed as obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r9.anchor: وروى ذلك عن إبن جريج والعزم بهذا المعنى مما ينسب إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r10.claim: On that interpretation, ʿazm is used for the thing resolved upon, and the construction makes the attribute qualify the described matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r10.anchor: والمراد به هنا المعزوم إطلاقا للمصدر على المفعول والإضافة من إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r11.claim: A grammatical alternative takes ʿazm as an active participle, “resolute matters,” through figurative attribution rather than an “in” genitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r11.anchor: وجوز أن يكون العزم بمعنى الفاعل أي عازم الأمور من عزم الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r12.claim: Another view understands the phrase as noble morals and the firm resolves of prudent people following the path of salvation; Abu Hayyan prefers obligatory matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r12.anchor: من مكارم الأخلاق وعزائم أهل الحزم السالكين طريق النجاة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r13.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r13.claim: Al-Mubarrad says ʿazm is ḥazm in Hudhayl's dialect, but Alusi rejects his suggestion that one word arose by changing the other’s initial consonant.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r13.anchor: وما قاله المبرد من أن العين قلبت جاء ليس بشيء لإطراد تصاريف كل من اللفظين

ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r14.claim: The closing clause gives the reason for obeying the preceding commands and emphasizes their special importance.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p89/r14.anchor: والجملة تعليل لوجوب الامتثال بما سبق وفيه اعتناء بشأنه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r1.claim: The command to endure concerns harm suffered while enjoining good and forbidding wrong; these duties and patience under their harm are obligatory matters or matters one must resolve to fulfill.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r1.anchor: يعني من الأذى، {إن ذلك من عزم الأمور} يريد الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر، والصبر على الأذى فيهما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r14.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r14.claim: Wahb says Luqman articulated twelve thousand branches of wisdom that people incorporated into their sayings, judgments, and maxims.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r14.anchor: قال وهب: تكلم لقمان باثنى عشر ألف باب من الحكمة، أدخلها الناس في كلامهم وقضاياهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r15.speaker: خالد الربعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r15.claim: Khalid al-Rabi recounts that Luqman's master asked for the best and then worst two morsels; both times Luqman brought the tongue and heart, good or bad according to their condition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p289/r15.anchor: قال خالد الربعي: كان لقمان عبدا حبشيا فدفع مولاه إليه شاة وقال: اذبحها وائتني بأطيب مضغتين منها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.claim: Ya bunayya is a diminutive expressing tenderness; Ibn Kathir, Hafs, al-Bazzi, and other readers differ on its yāʾ vowel in the cited places.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:13-16/r2.anchor: تصغير إشفاق، وقرأ ابن كثير هنا وفي { يبنى أقم الصلوة } بإسكان الياء

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r4.claim: Prayer completes the self; commanding right and forbidding wrong complete others; patience is needed through affliction, especially in this work.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r4.anchor: تكميلا لنفسك. { وأمر بالمعروف وانه عن المنكر } تكميلا لغيرك. { واصبر على ما أصابك } من الشدائد

BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r5.claim: That refers to patience or all the commands; resolute matters are obligations God decisively imposed, or matters that are firmly resolved.
BAYDAWI-FULL:31:16-17/r5.anchor: إشارة إلى الصبر أو إلى كل ما أمر به. { من عزم الأمور } مما عزمه الله من الأمور

BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r2.claim: Prayer is to be performed with all its limits and conditions; it saves and purifies the self and restrains wrongdoing because it turns toward the One God and away from all else.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r2.anchor: أي بجميع حدودها وشروطها ولا تغفل عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r3.claim: Prayer is second only to monotheism; the omission of almsgiving here signals Luqmān’s and his son’s detachment from worldly provision.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r3.anchor: ولهذا الإقبال والإعراض كانت ثانية التوحيد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r4.claim: Enjoining right completes one’s duty to others and is more comprehensive than merely forbidding wrong, since forbidding wrong does not itself entail performing good.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r4.anchor: عطف على ذلك تكميله لنفسه بتكميل غيره توفية لحق الخلق

BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r5.claim: People on life’s journey must protect companions: wrongdoing corrupts the shared vessel, and neglecting to restrain its corrupter can drown everyone.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r5.anchor: وكان فساد السفينة مغرقا لكل من فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r6.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r6.claim: Abū al-Aswad’s verse says to begin by correcting oneself; after one’s own soul gives up wrongdoing, one may rightly be called wise.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p19/r6.anchor: أبي الأسود رحمه الله تعالى : ابدأ بنفسك فانهها عن غيها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.claim: The sequence ‘patience and prayer’ in 2:45 differs because its addressees are unbelievers engrossed in worldly things, while Luqmān’s addressee is a believing ascetic.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r1.anchor: واختلاف المخاطب في الموضعين أوجب اختلاف الترتيبين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r2.claim: The counsel ends with patience, the key to all actions and abstentions.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r2.anchor: وجعل ختامه الصبر الذي هو ملاك الأعمال والتروك كلها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r3.claim: ‘That is among the matters requiring resolve’ names the counsel, especially patience, as decisive and obligatory matters on which one must be fully set; no religious community has leave to abandon them.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p20/r3.anchor: أي الأمور المقطوع بها المفروضة أو القاطعة الجازمة بجزم فاعلها

DURR-FULL:v6p523/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r3.claim: Enjoining right means calling to God's oneness, forbidding wrong means prohibiting associationism, and patience through resulting harm is among God's commanded duties.
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير رضي الله عنه في قوله {وأمر بالمعروف} يعني بالتوحيد {وانه عن المنكر} يعني عن الشرك

DURR-FULL:v6p523/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r4.claim: Patience through the harm caused by enjoining and forbidding is among the matters God determined and commanded.
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله {واصبر على ما أصابك} من الأذى في ذلك {إن ذلك من عزم الأمور}

DURR-FULL:v6p523/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r5.speaker: عمير بن حبيب
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r5.claim: Umayr advises his sons to avoid fools and, when enjoining right or forbidding wrong, prepare to endure harm and trust God's reward; trust makes hurt bearable.
DURR-FULL:v6p523/r5.anchor: عن أبي جعفر الخطمي رضي الله عنه أن جده عمير بن حبيب وكانت له صحبة أوصى بنيه

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r12.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r12.claim: Luqmān's counsels say to guard one's secret, avoid worldly temptation and excess, remember death and funerals, avoid burdening others, and seek refuge from harmful women, a satanic snare.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r12.anchor: ومن وصايا لقمان ما قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (لقمان سر خويش را ندداد ووصيت كردكه اى سر بسورها مروكة

BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r13.claim: Prayer perfects action after knowledge and belief; the earlier prohibition of shirk entailed tawḥīd, the first human duty.
BURSEVI:v7p61#4/r13.anchor: يا بنى أقم الصلواة} التي هي أكمل العبادات تكميلا لنفسك من حيث العمل بعد تكميلها

THALABI:v7p314/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p314/r7.claim: The resolute matters are obligations God commanded.
THALABI:v7p314/r7.anchor: أي الأمور الواجبة التي أمر الله بها

THALABI:v7p314/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p314/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses it as matters of resolve.

THALABI:v7p314/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p314/r9.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p314/r9.claim: Muqatil glosses it as matters that are right.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r3.claim: Maʿruf means monotheism in the command to enjoin it in 9:71 and 31:17; the source also groups 9:112.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p574/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن المعروف في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه : أحدها : التوحيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r2.claim: Al-Shura emphasizes the judgment with لام because patience combined with forgiveness is harder than patience alone in Luqman.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p593/r2.anchor: الصبر والغفران وهما أشدّ من الصبر وحده التي وردت في سورة لقمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1015/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1015/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1015/r3.claim: The author sees companionship as a recurring theme in Luqmān's counsel: the father guides his son, the son treats parents and others well, and people enjoin right and forbid wrong.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1015/r3.anchor: وكل وصية لقمان في المصاحبة مصاحبة الأب لابنه ينصحه ويعلمه ومصاحبة الإبن لأبيه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1109/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1109/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1109/r1.claim: Luqmān commends patience alone with إن; al-Shūrā adds forgiveness, harder when one is harmed, so it stresses the virtue with both إن and لام in لمن عزم الأمور.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1109/r1.anchor: زاد المغفرة على الصبر. أيها الأصعب على الإنسان أن يصبر أو يصبر يغفر إذا أُوذي؟ أن يصبر ويغفر أصعب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.claim: Luqman’s counsel shows Arabs that their own sages taught what the Qur’an teaches; it contrasts blind imitation of forefathers who followed Satan with the wise ancestors’ reflection, and condemns punishing children for conduct Luqman taught his son.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p106/r3.anchor: The succeeding verses refer to the wisdom of Luqmān and the advise he gave to his obedient son.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r1.claim: Prayer is the foremost and greatest expression of gratitude to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r1.anchor: It is the foremost and the greatest manifestation of gratitude to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r2.claim: All prophets and divine religions have taught people to pray.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r2.anchor: All prophets of God and all divine religions unanimously have taught people to pray.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r3.claim: The counsel means diligent prayer: he should pray himself, arrange for others to pray, and urge them to it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r3.anchor: not only adhere to the prayer himself, but make arrangements for others also

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r4.claim: Enjoining maʿrūf is the second expression of gratitude and connects a person to fellow people, whereas prayer connects him to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r4.anchor: It connects a person to his brethren. The prayer, on the other hand, connects a person to his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r5.claim: Maʿrūf covers fulfillment of rights, including charity, aid to orphans and needy people, help for neighbours, and familiar acts of kindness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r5.anchor: spending in the way of God, helping orphans, the destitute, neighbours and all other people in need

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r6.claim: Forbidding wrong means abstaining from conduct opposed to maʿrūf, such as stinginess, usurping rights, injustice, broken promises, and conceit.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r6.anchor: include stinginess, usurpation of rights, injustice, breaking promises, conceit etc.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r7.claim: Enjoining good and forbidding wrong bring hardship at every step, so they require patience and perseverance to make progress.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r7.anchor: if he does not exercise patience, he will not be able to take a single step ahead.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r8.claim: These tasks cannot be done half-heartedly; they demand full force, perseverance, and a willingness to stake one’s life on succeeding.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r8.anchor: these tasks cannot be carried out half-heartedly. Only those people can accomplish them who stand up with full force and perseverance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r9.claim: This is why Sūrat al-ʿAṣr also mentions steadfastness and patience in upholding the truth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p113/r9.anchor: In Sūrah al-‘Aṣr, it is precisely for this reason that showing steadfastness and patience on the truth is mentioned.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r2.claim: Luqmān’s counsel benefits everyone but has special force for leaders with political authority, since it prepares his son for leadership responsibilities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r2.anchor: they carry special significance for those who are in the position of leadership and have political authority.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r3.claim: Islahi describes Luqmān as a sage and political ruler, not a prophet, while seeing a general resemblance to the prophet David.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p115/r3.anchor: Luqmān was not a prophet; however he does have a general resemblance with the prophet David (sws).

NASHR:v2p289/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p289/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ opens the yāʾ in all six occurrences; Abū Bakr agrees at the Hūd occurrence, and al-Bazzī agrees at the last Luqmān occurrence, yā bunayya aqimi al-ṣalāh.
NASHR:v2p289/r1.anchor: روى حفص بفتح الياء في الستة

NASHR:v2p289/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p289/r2.speaker: قنبل
NASHR:v2p289/r2.claim: Qunbul lightens and gives sukūn to the yāʾ in the final Luqmān occurrence.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.claim: Luqman’s counsel warns against associating partners, commands kindness to parents and awareness of God, prayer, enjoining right, forbidding wrong and patience, and rejects pride while urging humility in walking and speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v21p139/r2.anchor: من التحذير من الإشراك ، ومن الأمر ببر الوالدين

JISHUMI:v8p5658/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5658/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5658/r1.claim: The command to enjoin right and forbid wrong also entails patience with the harm encountered in doing so.
